text:
Ana: quick follow-up from yesterday's postmortem — the memcache timeout alerts caused 3 noisy pages due to a cascade of low-volume backoffs. want to propose a short experiment to reduce paging noise without hiding real incidents.
Mike: +1. saw the pages — most were single-node blips with tiny user impact.
Jia: can you summarize the proposed change?
Ana: idea = add an snr (signal-to-noise) gating and a probabilistic dedupe layer. rules: only page if the metric crosses threshold AND snr_score >= 0.65 OR if it persists across 3 distinct hosts. fallback: still create tickets for anything we suppress.
Oliver: sounds reasonable. what's snr_score? how do we compute it?
Ana: rough calc: (error_rate_normalized * traffic_volume_normalized) / (1 + background_flapping_score). basically low-volume flaps get low snr. we can compute at query time from existing metrics.
Mike: implementation plan? will this need config + code change?
Ana: two parts: 1) alert rule change (prometheus rule + paging logic) — small PR. 2) a middleware in the pager service that computes snr and applies probabilistic dedupe for snr in [0.3,0.65]. set sampling so only 10-30% will page, but we record the suppressed alerts as incidents in the internal ticket stream.
Jia: what timelines? can we run as a 72h experiment?
Ana: propose: patch rule tomorrow (canary to staging), enable middleware in staging same day, deploy to prod as a 72h experiment on Mon 08:00 UTC. monitor page count, mean time to acknowledge, and customer-facing error rate.
Oliver: owner for rollout and rollback?
Ana: i'll own rollout + dashboarding. Mike will own rollback playbook and immediate fixes. Jia will validate runbook updates and ticketing.
SRE-Bot: incident summary (automated): https://incidents.redwood.ai/INC-2026-452. spike peaked at 2026-03-18T21:14Z, memcache miss rate +2.3x, paged 3 times.
Mike: can we codify the threshold tweak? drop the 95th -> 99th percentile? or keep but add the snr gate?
Ana: keep existing thresholds for now, add snr gate. for long-term we can revisit the percentile target after experiment.
Jia: sample rule snippet for the ops repo:
```
alert: memcache_latency_high
expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(memcache_latency_bucket[5m])) > 0.2
for: 5m
labels:
  severity: page
annotations:
  summary: "memcache 95th > 200ms"
# pager logic pseudocode:
# page_if: (snr_score >= 0.65) || (distinct_hosts >= 3) || (persisting_for >= 15m)
```
Ana: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-alerting/pull/412 — contains rule changes + test harness.
Oliver: monitor dashboards? what metrics are we tracking for success/failure?
Ana: pages/day (target -50% for memcache noise), suppressed_alerts_count (ensure we see them re-ingested), mttr (should not increase > 10%), user_error_rate (no regression).
Jia: add an audit log entry for every suppressed alert so CS can follow up if needed.
Ana: yes — middleware will log suppressed alerts to /logs/alerts/suppressed with ticket ref.
Mike: any risk of missing a real outage? crack open the rollback steps now so oncall has it: 1) disable middleware flag, 2) revert prometheus rule to previous commit, 3) escalate if pages spike.
Ana: documented rollback in PR and will post a short runbook update.
SRE-Bot: deployment window scheduled: Mon 2026-03-22 08:00 UTC -> 72h experiment. Reminder will post 1h before.
Oliver: ok good. follow-up action items: Ana -> rollout + dashboarding (due EOD Mon + 24h checkpoints), Mike -> rollback doc + runbook steps (due EOD today), Jia -> runbook + ticketing integration (due next Wed). will reconvene Thu after experiment for results. :thumbsup:
